tw-mn-wadena-buchan-np-camp-gold-1905.st: Two more accounts followed in August 1906. A New York clairvoyant staying at the Merchants hotel dug with a helper about half a mile up the track west of Wadena, claiming $900-1,000 lay under the double track, and found nothing. Then F. P. McQuillan of Aitkin, who had surveyed near Wadena before the rails were laid, wrote that along Union Creek, a little south of the track, he had seen a large hole in a high bank with no spoil around it, holding two barrels of fine dishes and bundles behind them he took for the gold; a local man asked him to keep quiet about it. He urged digging near Union Creek. So the record names four spots: the Peter Nelson farm east of Bluffton, Union Creek south of the track, the right of way near Verndale and the Wing River, and half a mile west of Wadena.

pinev: One mile from the Bluffton NP station (MnDOT roll 1348C) toward Wadena along the line, from the two MnDOT station points; the 1906 paper puts the main dig near Peter Nelson's home a mile on the Wadena side of Bluffton; farm not yet on a plat
Secondary tradition: right of way near Verndale and an old camp near the Wing River (Wadena Pioneer Journal, 16 Jun 1905)
Alternative: Union Creek a little south of the Northern Pacific track (McQuillan, Wadena Pioneer Journal, 30 Aug 1906); the creek's crossing of the line is not yet fixed.
